title: Introduce per-prompt tolerance profiles and auto-repair CI adapter
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: we have observed recurring false-positive regression failures for a small subset of prompt sets that are high-variance by design (edge-paraphrase cohorts, minority dialects). Default global gates are too brittle and force manual triage. This PR introduces a per-prompt tolerance profile and an automatic repair adapter in CI that (1) allows configurable per-prompt/slotted thresholds, (2) runs an automated lightweight repair loop (localized prompt perturbation + rerun) before firing a hard CI failure, and (3) surfaces a condensed failure report to aid human triage if auto-repair cannot resolve the regression. Summary: - New config: prompt_tolerance_profiles.yaml (schema described inline) that maps prompt_set ids to tolerated metric deltas and retry policies. - CI adapter: ci/adapters/per_prompt_tolerance_adapter.py that intercepts eval results in the eval-runner and applies the profile rules; if a violation is marginal it triggers the repair loop. - Repair loop: tools/repair/perturbation_repair.py attempts N randomized minimal edits (paraphrase swap, temperature jitter replay, seed-resample) and re-evaluates only the failing examples. - Reporting: ci/reports/compact_tolerance_reporter formats a one-page summary with repair attempts, before/after scores, and recommended actions. - Tests: unit and integration tests that simulate stable, flaky, and true-regression scenarios. Backwards compatibility: default profile is empty (global gate behaviour unchanged). Intended flow: on CI eval failure the adapter checks whether a profile exists for the prompt_set; if so it determines whether the observed delta is within the soft_tolerance window. If within soft_tolerance, the adapter runs the repair loop (bounded time budget). If repairs restore metrics above the release threshold, CI records a soft-fix annotation and continues; otherwise it escalates the failure with the compact report and links to the failing trace. Checklist: - [x] design doc attached (ENG-9842) - [x] schema + validation - [x] unit tests for adapter and repair primitives - [x] end-to-end smoke test in CI pipeline - [x] docs: add a short guide in docs/eval/gates.md - [x] changelog entry. Related: addresses flaky failures reported in ENG-9901 and reduces manual triage load. Performance/Cost: repair loop is limited by default to 10 examples and 3 attempts per example; runtime budget is configurable per profile. Security/privacy: repair operations run only on synthetic or anonymized traces; adapter respects PII flags in prompt metadata.

release_notes: Add per-prompt tolerance profiles and an optional auto-repair CI adapter that performs limited perturbation retries before failing evals. Configurable per-prompt policies reduce flaky CI failures for high-variance prompt sets and provide compact failure reports when human triage is required.
notes_for_oncall: If eval CI begins timing out after this change, check the per_prompt_tolerance_adapter timeout settings in eval-runner config (defaults: 60s repair budget per failing prompt_set). To temporarily disable the adapter, set EVAL_PER_PROMPT_TOLERANCE=0 in the pipeline environment.
